geometry_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant gesture but make the main mass more explicitly bent/continuous to reinforce a single readable rule across views.
Reduce the bend slightly to avoid a too-fragmented or awkward silhouette while keeping continuity.
Make the stepped upper mass more legible as a coherent inhabited section rather than a generic tiered stack.
Increase the number of authored section steps so the silhouette reads as a deliberate massing sequence with stronger hierarchy.
Introduce a real courtyard/public void to repair the weak ground threshold and give the neighborhood-living program a legible open-space figure.
Keep the courtyard bounded but substantial enough to function as usable public space.
Open the courtyard toward the access edge so the public threshold aligns with the site entry condition.
Make the new courtyard the root so the solid remains in ancestry but the public void becomes the governing spatial idea.

graph_edits.rationale: Preserve the dominant bar but make it a bent/profiled primary mass rather than a generic linear extrusion, so the silhouette better supports the observed four-view continuity and the neighborhood program.
Keep the long axis orientation stable while the primary mass is re-authored structurally.
Slightly strengthen the primary mass so the hierarchy reads more decisively as one dominant occupiable volume.
Deepen the carve so the frontage edge can become a legible public threshold instead of a shallow nick.
Align the carved void to the verified access side in the program frame to produce a frontage-responsive entry/court condition.
Add a stronger public void node so the mass gains a clear social court rather than relying on a weak surface subtraction.

rationale: The mass reads as one dominant stepped bar in all four views, so gesture clarity is decent and the silhouette is coherent. However, the street-edge response is weak: the blue frontage edge is not met with a convincing public void, undercut, or entry seam, and the main subtraction does not read as a legible neighborhood threshold. The section is more object-like than program-driven, with the stepped upper mass reading as generic terracing rather than an active mixed-use ground and supportive public space. It is repair-coherent and not visibly self-colliding, but the program contract for neighborhood living with an active ground edge is not satisfied strongly enough to hard-pass.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact stepped massing can support a neighborhood-scale public/commercial ground, but the key transferable idea is the calm upper profile over a more active base.

warnings: The verified access edge appears to call for a west-facing public threshold in program frame; the visible mass does not clearly align a legible opening to that edge.
Stepped upper form is acceptable as a silhouette device, but here it reads as a generic setback rather than a capacity-bearing section with public consequence.
Voids are present but remain too shallow/ambiguous to count as a strong public court or terrace.
